1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif face at comfortable size with reasonably open line spacing in headings, labels and body copy, though spacing is default rather than deliberately widened.

2.why: The interface text uses no italics or all-caps and short sentences, but the persistent monospace Logs panel grows into a dense unbroken block of code-like text on later steps.

3.why: The single centred card and stacked fields would reflow acceptably, but all evidence is at 1280px desktop width and the two-column recovery-code list and wide log strings suggest cramping on a phone.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Confirm your mobile number', 'Create a setup secret and add it manually to your authenticator app' and 'These codes are shown once. Store them safely.' are one line and plain.

5.why: Placeholders show expected formats ('+15551234567' for mobile, 'ABCD-EFGH-IJKL' for recovery code), although the 6-digit verification, authenticator code and manual secret fields have no example.

6.why: Every task screen requires reading only a heading plus one short sentence; the long log text is supplementary and not needed to proceed.

7.why: The 32-character setup secret and the 12-character recovery codes are shown as plain selectable text with no copy button or copy-all affordance, so hand transcription is the default.

8.why: No QR code appears anywhere; step 4 explicitly instructs the user to 'add it manually to your authenticator app'.

9.why: Standard labelled email and password inputs are used (and step 14 shows a filled password), but no autocomplete/one-time-code hints or password-manager support are demonstrable from the screenshots.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading and a filled blue primary button, but there is no step indicator or progress marker showing where the user is in the enrolment sequence.

11.why: Early screens ask for one action, but step 3 shows two buttons, step 6 shows two input fields, and the MFA settings screen offers verify, regenerate and log out simultaneously.

12.why: Some outcomes are stated plainly ('Recovery code accepted and used.', 'MFA is enabled. 8 recovery codes remain.'), but transitions like creating the secret or enabling MFA give no explicit 'what happens next' statement.

13.why: The user can re-send the verification code, retry sign-in, test codes and regenerate recovery codes freely, but there is no reveal/hide toggle and codes are 'shown once' with no way to view them again.

14.why: The only error seen, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming but names neither the actual problem nor any concrete fix.

15.why: No countdown timers, expiry warnings or session clocks are visible on any screen, so nothing rushes reading or code entry, though no explicit generous-time assurance is given either.
